summary: Episode 29: Inspired by his soaring kite, Tariq built a little water clock in the workshop courtyard — clay cups and hollow reeds that drip in turn to mark the hours, so the reading circle always knows when to gather. When the device kept time on its own, Salim taught him that puzzling out how the world is built is itself a way of drawing near to the One who built it — curiosity as a form of worship. That evening Salim again slipped an anonymous gift onto Noor's doorstep; she still cannot guess who her secret friend is.
open_threads: Noor still doesn't know who leaves the anonymous gifts at her door (Tariq knows it is Salim)
Tariq is discovering a love of building and understanding how things work — curiosity framed as worship
The reading circle keeps growing and now gathers by Tariq's water clock
Tariq's kite still flies over the district; the children who watch it now come to see his machines too
